premises.text: Talented professionals looking for jobs are reduced to resumes in a pile and struggle to stand out
premises.evidence_span: when we go look for a job, we get reduced to this. Just another resume and a pile of paper

premises.text: Sponsored low-stakes competitions, certifications, skills scores, leaderboards, and achievements let tech pros prove and build skills
premises.evidence_span: Guild is where social gaming meets career advancement for technology professionals

premises.text: Guild recommends jobs and gives application feedback on skill fit, applicant rank, and how to improve chances
premises.evidence_span: it is recommending jobs that I should be applying for, where I have a good chance of getting an interview

premises.text: Employers sponsor competitions and browse ranked participants' skills and backgrounds to invite passive candidates
premises.evidence_span: Guild also helps employers target and find the best people

premises.text: Free for professionals; monetize by charging employers; professionals and employers connect directly without agencies
premises.evidence_span: Guild is free for professionals. We monetize by charging employers

value.text: Technology professionals compete, connect, and advance their careers while employers find the best people
value.evidence_span: Professionals compete on Guild, connect, and advance their careers

causal_links.evidence_span: How can I make myself stand out above everyone else?
helps professionals advance their careers in ways that haven't been done before
helps employers target and find the best people
place for professionals and employers to connect directly

notes: Competition/skills/leaderboard/certification cascade folded for pros (§4.1.7); job-feedback kept as distinct career JTBD. Employer sourcing and commercial model separately revisable. Traction/beta counts excluded (§4.2).
